# core/ -- Rust Bridge Layer and Cython Utilities

The bridge between Rust engine and Python. Two independent binding paths coexist: legacy C FFI (for Cython consumers) and modern PyO3 (for Python consumers).

## Dual Binding Architecture

### Legacy path: C FFI (cbindgen) -- for Cython consumers

```
crates/{name}/src/ffi/
  --> cbindgen (build.rs)
  --> core/includes/{name}.h       (C headers)
  --> core/rust/{name}.pxd          (autogenerated, NEVER edit)
  --> core/rust/{name}.pyx          (hand-written enum re-exports)
  --> Python objects consumed by other .pyx modules
```

Only 4 crates generate FFI headers: `core`, `model`, `common`, `backtest`. Each has `cbindgen.toml` + `cbindgen_cython.toml` in its crate root. The `.pxd` files have cbindgen warning headers -- never edit manually.

### Modern path: PyO3 -- for Python consumers

`crates/pyo3/src/lib.rs` aggregates all ~20 crate `#[pymodule]` bindings into a single `nautilus_pyo3.cpython-*.so`. With `cython-compat` feature, all submodule attributes are re-exported at top level so Cython can `from nautilus_trader.core.nautilus_pyo3 import X`.

### Bridging pattern

Some `.pyx` modules re-export PyO3 functions for convenience. Example: `datetime.pyx` imports time-conversion functions from `nautilus_pyo3` and also provides C FFI-native functions (`unix_nanos_to_iso8601_cstr` from `rust/core.pxd`).

## Navigation: Where Rust Types Live

| Question | Where |
|----------|-------|
| Rust domain logic | `crates/{name}/src/` |
| PyO3 bindings | `crates/{name}/src/python/` |
| C FFI structs/enums | `rust/model.pxd` (~29 enums, price/qty/money structs) |
| C FFI component types | `rust/common.pxd` (ComponentState/Trigger, clocks, logging) |
| Python-level import | `nautilus_pyo3.pyi` (authoritative export surface) |

## Conventions

### cstr_to_pystr ownership model → `string.pxd:cstr_to_pystr`

`cstr_to_pystr(ptr, drop=True)` converts Rust `CString` to Python str and optionally frees Rust memory. The `drop` flag must be `False` when the pointer is borrowed (e.g., from a struct field Rust owns). Wrong `drop` value causes either memory leak (`False` on `CString::from_raw`) or UB (`True` on borrowed pointer).

### HIGH_PRECISION conditional → `rust/model.pxd`

`DEF HIGH_PRECISION = True` with `IF`/`IF not` blocks switches between 64-bit and 128-bit fixed-point widths. Compile-time decision baked into `.so`. Build script sets env var (default: true, except Windows).

### Enum import pattern

Cython: `cimport` from `rust/*.pxd`. Python: import from `nautilus_pyo3`. Both resolve to same underlying C-level enum values.

### When to use which binding path

| Scenario | Path |
|----------|------|
| New `.pyx` code needing Rust types | `cimport` from `rust/*.pxd` |
| Pure Python needing Rust types | Import from `nautilus_trader.core.nautilus_pyo3` |
| New Rust type Cython needs | Add FFI in `crates/{name}/src/ffi/`, rebuild to regenerate headers |
| New Rust type Python-only needs | Add PyO3 in `crates/{name}/src/python/`, update `nautilus_pyo3.pyi` |

## Module Boundary

Lowest layer -- no imports from other nautilus_trader subpackages (except the Rust extension). Everything else imports from here. The `rust/` subdirectory is purely FFI declarations and enum re-exports; no application logic.
